problems.statement: The spring service change cut recovery (layover) time on 21 of 38 routes to fund Route 51, so late inbound buses cannot recover and leave terminals late; this propagates lateness across those routes.

Construction lane reductions on Halvorsen Avenue and Bridgeport Road (from 2026-04-20) roughly doubled running times through the work zones on five routes, causing a second, larger OTP drop on those routes. It compounds with the recovery cut on the same routes.
Operator absenteeism rising 40% is the main cause of the OTP decline (the client's explanation).

The reported 40% absence increase is largely a measurement artifact: ShiftLine (live 2026-03-30) began recording partial-day absences that the legacy process never entered, while full-day absences rose only 1.1%.
Operator-availability problems (missed trips, late pull-outs, extraboard use) have not worsened, so there is no real dispatch-side shortage driving lateness.

Early-leave occurrences are higher among operators on recovery-cut routes, possibly because of fatigue or no breaks from the layover cut. This is confounded by seniority, age, route length and garage, and has no pre-April baseline.
The OTP data are unreliable because of AVL measurement error or a definition change.
Passenger demand, boarding or dwell-time growth is causing the delays.
Garage-specific problems (North Garage staffing) explain the decline.

causalClaims.to: Late terminal departures and OTP decline on Groups A and B
Longer work-zone running times and a second OTP drop on Group A

causalClaims.from: Timing coincidence of absence rise and OTP drop in April

actions.action: Restore recovery time on the recovery-cut routes (or add buses or runs to fund it), prioritising the five construction-corridor routes. Re-time those five routes to the new work-zone running times.
actions.rationale: This addresses the two mechanisms with the strongest evidence, the recovery cut and the construction delay, and does not depend on any unconfirmed explanation.

actions.action: Re-time the construction-corridor routes using the measured work-zone running times (about +6.5 and +5.5 min). Ask the city about traffic-management or signal and bus-priority measures.
actions.rationale: Running time in the work zones roughly doubled, so schedules there are unachievable as written.

actions.action: Respond to the May schedule grievance and engage the union on layover and break conditions.
actions.rationale: The grievance has gone unanswered and the layover issue is documented. Responding is low-cost and reversible.

actions.action: Report absenteeism to the board using like-for-like full-day absences (+1.1%), and correct the 40% figure.
actions.rationale: The 40% figure is a recording artifact. The board and policy decisions should rest on comparable data.

actions.action: Roll out the tougher attendance policy, with discipline at 3 occurrences in 90 days counting all ShiftLine-recorded occurrences.
actions.rationale: It targets a non-cause and would discipline operators for partial-day entries that were never counted before. It would sour labour relations while the schedule grievance is open.

actions.action: Build a union communications plan whose message is that absenteeism is the cause of the OTP decline.
actions.rationale: The evidence contradicts the message, and it would damage credibility.

actions.action: Add extraboard operators or run a dispatch fix to reduce the absence-board burden.
actions.rationale: Missed trips and late pull-outs are unchanged, so this addresses no demonstrated problem.

actions.action: Study early-leave causes (fatigue, no breaks, health) on recovery-cut routes after layovers are restored.
actions.rationale: The early-leave link to layovers is confounded, so it is worth examining but not acting on yet.

nextEvidence: Group A OTP split by recovery cut versus construction, e.g. modelled or pilot results from restoring recovery on a subset of routes, to size the separate contributions and test the effect.
Early-leave rates on recovery-cut versus other routes controlled for seniority, route length and garage, plus any pre-April sick-leave data.
Run-by-run analysis of how lateness propagates through the day on recovery-cut routes (arrival lateness at terminals versus layover available), to size how much recovery to restore.
output.summary: The OTP drop (82% to 71%) is explained by two schedule and road factors, not absenteeism. The April recovery-time cut on 21 routes made late buses depart terminals late (Groups A and B fell; Group C did not). The April 20 construction on five of those routes roughly doubled work-zone running times and added a second, larger drop. The 40% absence rise is mostly a ShiftLine recording artifact: full-day absences rose 1.1%. Missed trips, late pull-outs and extraboard use are unchanged. Restore layover and re-time the construction routes. Do not roll out the tougher attendance policy.
